note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em. NOTE ON THE FRAMES: drag_check.segments_redrew came back FALSE on this capture (cloud_redrew true, d_az 0.7500 = expected). It is a false negative of the probe, not stale frames: the probe reads seg3_src.data.xs[0][0], and that point IS the nu vertex (state.json segments xs[0][0]/ys[0][0] = 36.73/-72.93 = main_vertex u/v exactly), so during the vertex-centred sweep it sat ON the rotation centre and an azimuth rotation cannot move it -- seg_u went 9.88e-7 -> 1.03e-6, i.e. zero to zero. The same source reads u = 36.73 for that point under the later shower-framed camera, so seg3_src does reproject. Judgements below are made off frames I confirmed move. shw 2011 (244.3 MeV, 4 seg, 46.0 cm, conn 3) is UNDER-CLUSTERED and the missing piece is named: shw 2013 (64.8 MeV, one 17.8 cm segment, same cluster 2) sits at dist 10.4 cm and angle 2.5 deg from 2011's start -- the IDENTICAL distance and angle as accepted member 2014, so on the acceptance plot the two markers coincide -- and the reco threw it out with conn3_unreachable (walk_exclude). Both azimuths show why that is wrong: at az+085 the 2011 skeleton and the 2013 skeleton run parallel, 1-2 cm apart, up the middle of ONE continuous diffuse charge cloud from a common lower end; at az-055 the same two skeletons overlap in the same cloud. Two skeletons, one shower. Pricing them as a pi0 pair gives 16.7 MeV (axis) / 5.8 MeV (vertex) at 7.6 / 2.7 deg -- collinear, which no pi0 can be, and which is itself the proof they are one object. 2013 marked IN. Vertex is good: at both azimuths the star is the clean apex of a two-track V and the shower start sits ~4 cm off the muon (2048, 187.1 cm, pdg 13, correctly unowned) at 91.8 deg. Left alone deliberately: 2008 (pdg 2212, 32.1 cm) at 167 deg behind the start, and 62046 (50.1 MeV, 14.6 cm) at 142 deg behind it -- both outside the cone. Small on-axis stubs I noticed but did not mark: 17020 (0.6 cm) at 30.7 cm/12.6 deg -- the only non-member circle inside the acceptance window -- and 22025 (0.9 cm) at 49.2 cm/2.1 deg, 27030 (1.5 cm) at 53.1 cm/7.5 deg beyond it. Looked at 2 of 23 showers properly; 29040 (43.3 MeV) and 28031 (30.2 MeV) are 72-85 cm away in the opposite hemisphere and I only checked they are not near 2011, and the 18 skipped by the scope rule are all under 20 MeV.
